# Highlands Road Trip

Seven days in a hired estate car with Ines, looping north from Inverness and back. About 1,150 km in total. These are the day notes I typed up each evening, so they ramble a bit.

## Day one: Inverness to Ullapool

Picked up the car at the airport at 10 am. The hire desk tried to sell us extra insurance for the single track roads, which we skipped. Drove west through Garve, stopping at the Rogie Falls for the salmon ladder, though it was too early in the year for any jumping. Arrived in Ullapool in time for fish and chips on the harbour wall. The guesthouse was the Ferry View, room 3, with a window onto the loch. Breakfast was good but the shower ran cold after five minutes.

## Day two: Ullapool to Lochinver

Short distance but slow, the coast road is single track almost the whole way. Passing places everywhere, and most drivers wave. Stopped at Achmelvich beach, which has white sand and water the colour of a swimming pool, and far too cold to go in for more than a minute. Lochinver has a pie shop that everyone talks about. The venison and cranberry pie was worth the queue. Stayed at a B&B called Glencanisp Lodge Cottage with a peat fire.

## Day three: Lochinver to Durness

Long day of driving. Kylesku bridge in sunshine, then up past Scourie to Durness. We walked into Smoo Cave, a huge sea cave with a waterfall inside, and took the little boat trip to the inner chamber. Hostel bunk room for the night, which Ines did not enjoy. Note for next time: the hostel kitchen has no oven, only two hobs.

## Day four: Durness to Tongue

The plan was to visit Balnakeil craft village in the morning. Most of it was closed because it was out of season. Drove along the north coast to Tongue in heavy rain. We skipped the Dunnet Head detour to save energy for the next day. Stayed at the Tongue Hotel, which had a drying room for our boots, the best feature of the whole week.

## Day five: Tongue to Aviemore

Cut inland through the Flow Country, miles of bog and almost no other cars. Saw two golden eagles near Altnaharra, or at least we are fairly sure they were golden eagles and not buzzards. Long drive south to Aviemore. We stayed in a log cabin at the Rothiemurchus estate, booked through a friend of Ines, with a wood burner and a hot tub that we used in the dark at 10 pm.

## Day six: Cairngorms

A day out of the car. Walked the loop around Loch an Eilein, about 7 km and flat, then took the funicular up Cairn Gorm, which was in cloud, so we saw nothing at the top. In the afternoon we had a tour booked at the Speyside distillery, but we cancelled it because Ines had a migraine, and spent the evening reading in the cabin instead.

## Day seven: back to Inverness

Stopped at Culloden battlefield on the way back. The visitor centre is very well done and sobering. Dropped the car back with a quarter tank, which cost us a refuelling charge we could have avoided by filling up in Nairn.

## Lessons

Book the single track sections for mornings, when the roads are quiet. Bring midge spray even in April. Fill the tank before dropping the hire car back.
